MODERN SCHOOLTraditional setting
Earlscliffe offers students aged 15-19 years old a ‘home from home’ environment which is welcoming, safe and comfortable. The small community of around 150 students from all over the world truly is a global village in which cultural exchange, sporting opportunity and meaningful community service flourish. Personalised pastoral care and support are offered without being intrusive.
GLOBAL LEARNERSProudly international
With years of experience welcoming international students, Earlscliffe specialises in helping young people from around the world settle, grow and excel.
Students benefit from the distinctive Earlscliffe approach: small classes, regular progress testing and a strong emphasis on academic enrichment and university preparation.
We proudly celebrate 48 nationalities, enriching the school with global perspectives, friendships and cultures.
‘My favourite thing is the atmosphere in the school. Everyone works so hard to make you feel that you belong here.’

pageCache.pageTitle: Football Academy in partnership with Tottenham Hotspur | Earlscliffe
pageCache.text:
Football and academic excellence, intelligently combined.
Study for internationally recognised UK qualifications with our full-time football and academic pathway.
The Partnership
The Earlscliffe Football Academy, delivered in partnership with Tottenham Hotspur Football Club, offers a unique full-time pathway that intelligently combines high-quality football coaching with serious academic study.
Open to boys and girls of all abilities aged 15–19, the programme is designed for ambitious young players who understand that education and sport are not in competition meaning students do not have to choose between sport and study.
With Spurs coaching sessions embedded alongside a full academic timetable, students develop as technically proficient, tactically intelligent and mentally resilient footballers, while also earning recognised UK qualifications and preparing for university entrance, including pathways to US higher education.
See the Programme in Action
Watch how Earlscliffe and Tottenham Hotspur have created a programme where football development and academic ambition work together.
For September 2026 entry, Earlscliffe is offering full scholarships for this programme which includes:
Daily Football Coaching
Structured sessions every day of the week, from technical skills and tactical shape to strength, conditioning and video analysis.
UK Qualifications
A-levels, Business Diploma, GCSEs, and other qualifications studied alongside football, delivered by Earlscliffe’s specialist teaching team.
Authentic Club Immersion
Matchday experiences, visits to the Spurs Training Centre, and a genuine connection to one of the world’s most recognised football clubs.
University Pathway Support
Dedicated guidance for students targeting US universities, including SAT preparation and scholarship-focused advice.
About Tottenham Hotspur Football Club
Tottenham Hotspur is one of the most storied clubs in English and European football, competing in the Premier League and playing home matches at their state-of-the-art stadium in north London. Founded in 1882, the club has a proud tradition of developing technically gifted players who excel at the highest levels of the game.
Spurs have consistently been at the forefront of football development, with an academy and coaching infrastructure that is recognised globally. Their commitment to the technical and tactical education of young players makes them an exceptional partner for a programme designed to develop the complete footballer.
For students joining this programme, the Tottenham Hotspur name is not merely a badge. It is an active presence: a full-time coach on campus, regular access to Spurs facilities, and an immersive experience of what a Premier League football environment looks and feels like.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pearson Extended Certificate in Sport | Earlscliffe
pageCache.text:
The Pearson BTEC Level 3 Extended Certificate in Sport, is equivalent to one A-level, combining exams, coursework, and practical assessment.
This qualification is widely recognised by universities and employers. It works particularly well for students who are practical, motivated by sport, and interested in turning that passion into future study or a career.
One of the biggest strengths of the course is that it blends academic understanding with real-world application. Students are assessed through a mixture of exams, coursework and practical tasks, which suits learners who thrive beyond purely exam-based subjects.
The core units delivered are:
Unit 1: Anatomy and Physiology
Students develop a strong understanding of how the body works during sport and exercise, including the muscular, skeletal, cardiovascular and respiratory systems. This underpins progression into sport science, physiotherapy, PE teaching and related degrees.
Unit 2: Fitness Training and Programming for Health, Sport and Wellbeing
A highly applied unit where students learn how to assess individuals, understand lifestyle factors, and design safe and effective training programmes. This links directly to careers in coaching, fitness and health-related fields.
Unit 3: Professional Development in the Sports Industry
This unit focuses on careers, employability and progression. Students explore different pathways in sport, complete a personal skills audit, develop a career action plan, and take part in interview and application-style activities. It’s excellent preparation for both university and the workplace.
Unit 5: Application of Fitness Testing
A very hands-on unit where students administer, analyse and evaluate fitness tests, then provide feedback to performers. This develops confidence, communication skills and applied sport science knowledge.
The qualification is ideal for students who:
Alongside the academic lessons, students receive approximately 4–6 hours per week of structured practical sport and physical training, including performance sessions, strength and conditioning, and competitive opportunities.
Practical elements are fully integrated into Units 2 and 5, ensuring students are consistently applying theory to real sporting contexts.
It is also possible to deliver the qualification over one year for students who are with us for a shorter period.

pageCache.text:
Enabling international learners to compete at the highest level. At Earlscliffe, we believe that language should never be the limiting factor in a student’s academic success.
Our English Centre of Excellence provides specialist English provision designed specifically for international students studying the British curriculum. More than just exam preparation, our programme offers a rich, immersive and personalised approach to English that empowers students to thrive both inside and outside the classroom.
While we proudly prepare students for internationally recognised qualifications such as IELTS and a full suite of Cambridge English exams (PET, FCE, CAE and CPE), our support goes far beyond test technique.
As an accredited Cambridge centre, the school can offer students the opportunity to sit these exams right here on campus, removing the stress and disruption of travelling to external test centres.
Our English Centre of Excellence focuses on developing:
This holistic approach ensures students can fully access their GCSE and A-level subjects, express their ideas clearly, and perform at their true academic potential.
English for Academic Purposes (EAP)

Dedicated English Language Experts
Language learning at Earlscliffe is designed to be immersive, dynamic and deeply relevant. Under the leadership of Miss Lana Golubeva, the English Language Centre of Excellence has been expanded to not only teach English, but to bring it vividly to life.
Miss Golubeva and her team bring a wealth of international experience and an infectious passion for language learning. They champion a curriculum built around the interests, ambitions and everyday experiences of our students. Whether a student is pursuing GCSEs or A-levels, their English lessons are carefully tailored to complement both their academic studies and personal passions.
Engaging Lessons
Our lessons use clear imagery and visual resources to make new vocabulary memorable and meaningful. From discussions on global business trends to debates on modern art, every class is infused with relevance, creativity and energy.
Students are encouraged to speak, question, debate and collaborate. Lessons frequently involve:
These experiences not only strengthen language skills but also develop essential life skills such as critical thinking, collaboration and self-confidence.

Additional English Pathways
To further support confident communication and performance, students can also access additional English enrichment pathways, including:
We are delighted to offer LAMDA Public Speaking as a one-year course for Year 12 students. This course is more than just a qualification. It is a powerful platform for students to build essential confidence in public speaking, alongside independent research skills and the ability to craft compelling arguments and presentations, skills that are invaluable in both academic and professional settings.
These programmes help students develop fluency, clarity, and presence in spoken English, building skills that are invaluable for presentations, interviews and university life.
English Speaking Board (ESB)
From Beginners to Top Universities
Whether a student arrives with beginner-level English or is aiming for top IELTS scores to access the very best universities in the UK, the English Language Centre of Excellence provides the structure, support and inspiration needed to succeed.

University preparation at Earlscliffe is structured, specialist and continuous.
Through The Careers Institute, we offer:
The majority of our students will be looking to progress to a top university, either in the UK or abroad. Our university and careers guidance will open the conversation about their aims and talents soon after their arrival.
We also run a series of activities and events that bring awareness to a wide range of available future pathways. As the students’ time at Earlscliffe progresses, they will be guided towards their target university or career, composing a powerful personal statement and building an accompanying portfolio of relevant experiences.
If a student is called for an interview by a university, they will first be given a mock interview at Earlscliffe.
Partnerships offered with Dukes Plus.
Earlscliffe students have access, at no additional cost, to the following partnerships offered through Dukes Plus:
Oxbridge Applications
The highest standard of UK & Oxbridge application support, empowering students to succeed in applications to Oxford, Cambridge, and other top UK universities, with a 73% success rate.

The Medic Portal partners with schools to deliver UCAT prep, interview training, insight days, personal statements and more.
Lawyer Portal
The Lawyer Portal works with schools to deliver expert talks, workshops and online programmes. Partnered with top law firms, students are equipped with clear guidance on legal career routes, applications and the skills they need to succeed.

Earlscliffe made the transition from school to University so much easier.
UCAS (Universities and Schools Admissions Service) Guidance
Students apply to their choice of UK universities in the Michaelmas Term of their final year.
However, the application process begins when students start at Earlscliffe. We use Unifrog, an online platform, to help students research, plan and prepare for their chosen post-Earlscliffe pathway. In the Trinity Term of Year 12, students are taken off timetable for several different events to prepare for university applications. As with everything at Earlscliffe, a personalised approach is provided for university applications.
Students applying to universities in the UK will submit applications to up to five institutions through UCAS and receive comprehensive guidance in selecting appropriate courses and universities.

UCAS Guidance Steps
From September of their first year at Earlscliffe, students actively start exploring potential university pathways and applications.
Every student is provided with a Unifrog account, an invaluable tool for researching potential future pathways, universities, and courses worldwide. Dedicated time is allocated to guide students through this research and help them make informed decisions about their academic future.
In the final term of Year 12, students are given off-timetable sessions to focus on crafting their personal statements. During this time, they also plan crucial summer activities such as work experience and subject-specific research, which are vital for strengthening their applications. Specialists are readily available to provide individual assistance and run smaller, subject-specific personal statement workshops to help students articulate their passions and achievements effectively.
For students aspiring to study outside the UK, this allocated time also allows them to work on their international university applications, with full support and guidance from our experienced staff.
Students applying to Oxford or Cambridge (Oxbridge), or for highly competitive courses such as Medicine, Dentistry, or Veterinary Science, will submit their applications by the October deadline. All other UCAS applications are typically submitted to universities in November. We understand that some students may join us later in the academic year, and, for these students, we provide individualised support to ensure they are fully prepared and can meet the final UCAS deadline at the end of January.
Once applications have been submitted, we work with students to ensure they choose the most suitable Firm and Insurance choices for their final two UCAS choices. Alongside this, a rich programme of academic enrichment and leadership opportunities ensures that each student’s ambitions are not only nurtured but surpassed. This focused approach leads to excellent outcomes.
Our students progress to leading universities in the UK, including top Russell Group institutions, as well as prestigious universities across Europe and North America. Earlscliffe is a community of intellectual curiosity and global perspective. We cultivate joyful, inquisitive learners who engage deeply with their studies and with the world around them. Here, ambition is not simply encouraged, it is translated into purposeful action, underpinned by responsibility, integrity and respect.
Students are encouraged to be ambitious, connected and exceptional, developing into thoughtful, reliable individuals ready to contribute meaningfully in a complex world. Earlscliffe offers a rare balance of focus, community and opportunity, where students flourish and prepare to shape their global future.

When we first acquired our main building in 2011, it stood empty and disused, but we could already see what it might become. A year later that vision became reality — thanks to determination, hard work and a close sense of purpose, all of which we encouraged in generations of our students.
We created Earlscliffe to offer something different from larger institutions: a school where every student is known, supported and challenged to achieve the best. Studying away from home is a big step, and that understanding shapes everything we do — from our teaching and university guidance to the pastoral care that helps students feel secure, confident and ready to thrive. We strongly feel that a ‘layering’ of experiences, throughout these pivotal years in a young person’s life, contributes hugely to the adult character and outlook they eventually assume. Such experiences vary from public speaking to volunteering in the wider, local community, and from hearing global politicians at the LSE to marvelling at a Mozart piano concert at London’s Wigmore Hall.
As we often say — to our own children as well as to our students — be ambitious, and make an impact.
Despite being a history teacher, it was a Nobel Prize-winning physicist’s infectious energy and drive that once inspired Tim’s approach to working with young people, when Richard Feynman stated that ‘the highest forms of understanding we can achieve are laughter and human compassion.’
We would love to meet you at Earlscliffe to talk about vision, not for a building anymore, but for a future — yours.
Tim and Julie Fish Founders

Support and wellbeing
At Earlscliffe, students thrive with strong academic and emotional support. This includes close teamwork between staff, a qualified school nurse, and small classes with personalised attention.
We know that students behave better, achieve higher grades and are more engaged in school life if they are supported, not only academically, but also emotionally.
Therefore, we provide a wrap-around approach to caring for our students that includes clear communication between the boarding house staff and the teaching teams, the nurse, the special educational needs team and fully trained mental health staff.
Earlscliffe also has a Nurse, who can assess and advise on minor injuries and ailments (i.e. coughs, colds, headaches, allergies). They can also offer psychological support and make referrals to other agencies such as the local doctor, counsellor, minor injuries unit, optician, physiotherapist and dentist.
Support for Students with Special Educational Needs.
At Earlscliffe, every student matters and we aim to ensure that every student succeeds.
Our goal is to develop independent-minded young men and women, eager to continue their studies and take their places as thoughtful citizens of the world. We believe that in the process of preparing and guiding young people towards intellectual growth, the beginning is everything. We seek to develop students’ abilities to work effectively, to communicate articulately, to approach life with a sense of competence. We are a close-knit community, working together to cultivate young minds and hearts.
We understand that every student is different, and that some students will need a little extra support to help them reach their full potential. We welcome students with Special Educational Needs, mental or physical health issues, and those for whom English is a second language.
We also have experience in educating students with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). We have well-developed monitoring systems to assess and track all students’ progress. This ensures that barriers to learning are quickly identified and minimised.
Earlscliffe has a Senco and Deputy Senco (Special Educational Needs Coordinator), who work closely with both teachers and students to plan appropriate levels of support. Please tell us your needs when you apply, so we can discuss how the college can support you.

A rigorous A-level education, designed for international learners
With an average class size of 7 and dedicated UCAS support, our A-level programme equips students with the qualifications, skills and confidence to secure places at the world’s leading universities.
The programme runs over two years (UK Years 12 and 13). Students typically study four A-level subjects — including their native language where possible — alongside the Extended Project Qualification (EPQ), an independent research project that develops the critical thinking and academic writing skills expected at university level.
English for Academic Purposes (EAP) is embedded throughout every lesson, and non-native English speakers can also complete their IELTS qualification if required. Every student receives 1:1 UCAS university counselling from experienced staff who have guided hundreds of students to their first-choice university destinations
We also offer the Pearson BTEC Level 3 Extended Certificate in Sport, equivalent to one A-level, combining exams, coursework, and practical assessment and providing a pathway to university and sports-related careers.
A-level subjects offered
Students typically choose four subjects from the following list. Subject availability may vary each year. Students are guided towards combinations that align with their strengths and university ambitions.
Art & Design
Lessons
6 hours total per week.
Practical subject:
Entry Requirements
Students are welcome to join the A-level course even if they have not previously studied Art formally. What is most important is that they bring curiosity, interest, ambition, and creativity to their work. While having a GCSE in Art (or equivalent of at least two years’ study and practice) is advantageous, it is not essential. Students may also have developed their skills through private lessons, extracurricular activities, or study in another school system. Above all, enthusiasm, self-motivation, and a willingness to experiment and explore ideas are integral to success in this subject.
Course Aim
Our A-Level Art course invites students to:
By integrating hands-on experimentation with analytical reflection and encouraging both creative risk-taking and personal expression, our course ensures alignment with the AQA A-Level Art & Design objectives. Students will develop both the creative independence and critical awareness required for success in their Personal Investigation and externally set assignments.
Course & Assessment overview
Year 1
In the first year, students work primarily in a single coursework book, developing a strong foundation in a wide range of media, materials, and techniques. The aim is to establish the creative and technical skills that will underpin their success in the full A-Level (Year 2).
Throughout the year, students will sit two internal assessments and a mock exam, each providing the opportunity to take ideas from their bookwork into a practical outcome completed under timed conditions.
All work is assessed in line with the AQA marking criteria, with feedback focusing on developing students’ ability to:
This structured progression ensures that students are both technically prepared and creatively confident by the time they enter the A-Level exam year.
investigate and develop ideas,
experiment with and refine media and materials,
record and analyse observations,
and present personal, meaningful outcomes.
Year 2
Career and Opportunities
The creative industries are among the fastest-growing and most dynamic sectors of the global economy, offering a wide range of well-paid and fulfilling careers. Fields such as architecture, fashion, graphic design, film, advertising, marketing, gaming, product design, animation, and the media all rely on highly skilled and imaginative individuals.
Studying Art at A-level not only develops technical ability and visual literacy but also fosters problem-solving, innovation, and independent thinking—skills that employers and universities consistently rank as highly valuable across all sectors.
At Earlscliffe, we go beyond the classroom by connecting students directly with the creative industries. Throughout the course, visiting professionals share their expertise through talks, workshops, and mentoring sessions, giving students invaluable insight into the realities of building a creative career and the opportunities available in this diverse field.
By combining rigorous academic preparation with real-world exposure, our students are well equipped to progress to top universities, art schools, and design programmes, and to pursue careers that are both financially rewarding and personally meaningful.
Biology
Lessons
6 hours total per week.
Practical subject:
Entry Requirements
We would expect that applicants to this course would have grades 9-4 in British GCSE Biology/Science and Mathematics or equivalent grade/mark in their national system of secondary education.
Course Aim
Course & Assessment overview
Year 1
Paper 1: Lifestyle, Transport, Genes and Health. This first topic for this paper involves the study of the functioning of the circulatory system and the importance of lifestyle choices to health. Whilst the second topic explores the exchange and transport of materials, DNA, protein synthesis enzymes and monohybrid inheritance within the context of the genetic disease Cystic Fibrosis.
Paper 2: Development, Plants and the Environment. This first topic for this paper involves the study of the development of multicellular organisms from single cells to complex individuals. The second topic focuses on the biodiversity and wealth of natural resources used by humans.
Year 2
Paper 1: The Natural Environment and Species Survival. This paper involves the study of topics studied for AS Biology plus a topic that builds an appreciation for photosynthesis as a process that underpins the majority of ecosystems. The second topic looks at the wide variety of techniques used by forensic pathologists to determine the identity and the time and cause of death in organisms, including humans.
Paper 2: Energy, Exercise and Co-ordination. This paper involves the study of topics studied for AS Biology plus a topic that is centred on the physiological adaptations that enable animals and humans to undertake strenuous exercise. The second topic considers how the working of the nervous system enables us to see.
Paper 3: General and Practical Applications in Biology. This paper involves the interpretation and analysing experimental results/data based upon the topics 1 -8. There is also one section with questions based upon a pre-released scientific article.
Career and Opportunities
By studying Biology at school or college students are opening the door to a wide variety of rewarding careers. As well as learning about how organisms works, students will get a broad training in skills that all employers value – an ability to grasp concepts quickly, a determination to find coherent answers, not to mention problem solving, analytical, evaluation, mathematical and IT skills. “A” grades in Biology are highly valued by leading British universities. Careers in Biology may be very versatile and literally “mind-blowing”, but if you have chosen Medicine, Veterinary Science, Biochemistry or Zoology, or even management and finance, the skills developed by studying Biology are still highly regarded.

Students do chemistry mostly to go on to study Medicine and do research at prestigious universities. Along with Engineering these are the best paid science related jobs all over the world. Chemical engineers develop novel materials that improve our quality of life and new batteries to fuel our various electrical devices. Chemists work for pharmaceutical companies to develop new drugs to cure diseases and help fight bugs that would destroy our crops. Molecular biologists want to understand the way living cells operate and study DNA, proteins and their reactions. A Programme Designed for Success
The Academic Integration programme is an immersive academic and cultural experience for international students aged 15–18. It can be taken for one month, one term, or two terms during the academic year.
Students follow a balanced curriculum designed to strengthen subject knowledge, improve English, and build confidence for future international study. Beyond the classroom, they are fully integrated into school life, taking part in sports, creative activities and cultural experiences alongside full-time students — gaining a genuine insight into British boarding school life.
Core subjects include:
Mathematics
Sciences
Humanities
Creative subjects
English language
Key features include:
Comprehensive curriculum: Students will study a balanced array of subjects, including mathematics, humanities, sciences, and English language.
Sports and cultural activities: Students will participate in a wide range of sports and cultural programmes. These activities provide opportunities to build friendships, develop skills, and immerse themselves in the rich heritage of England.
Premium accommodation: Participants will enjoy high-quality, en-suite accommodation in comfort.
Immersive boarding school experience: Students will study and engage alongside peers from the academic year programme, offering an authentic and inclusive educational journey.
Cambridge exam: Students will take the Cambridge exam at the end of their stay
Flexible opportunities: Students can extend their experience by combining this programme with one of Earlscliffe’s engaging summer courses in July.
